Thought: I need to determine the correct relationship between charge density (ρ) and detonation pressure (p_{C-J}) for explosives. This is a chemistry question related to explosives and detonation theory.

In explosive detonation theory, the Chapman-Jouguet (C-J) pressure is related to the square of the charge density. This relationship is derived from detonation physics where the detonation pressure is proportional to the square of the detonation velocity, which itself is proportional to the charge density.

The standard relationship is p_{C-J} ∝ ρ², which means that if the density doubles, the detonation pressure increases by a factor of 4.

Looking at the options, this corresponds to option A: p_{C-J} ∝ ρ²
